title: Penile erectile tissue anatomy
description: Two dorsal cavernous bodies and one ventral spongiosum carry arterial, neural and urethral pathways through the penis.

questions.question: What are the three erectile bodies of the penis?
questions.answer: Two paired corpora cavernosa form the main dorsal erectile cylinders. A single corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra and expands into the glans.

questions.question: What does the tunica albuginea do in erectile tissue?
questions.answer: It is a dense connective-tissue covering around erectile compartments, particularly strong around the corpora cavernosa.

questions.question: What are the paired corpora cavernosa?
questions.answer: Two dorsal longitudinal erectile cylinders that unite in shaft and separate proximally as crura. Function: Primary rigid erectile compartment.

questions.question: Where is the tunica albuginea located?
questions.answer: Strong fibrous sheath encasing cavernosa, with distinct collagen layers. Function: Resists expansion and aids venous occlusion.

questions.question: What is the function of the deep penile arteries?
questions.answer: Function: Feed cavernosal tissue. Internal pudendal branches traveling within each corpus cavernosum.
